title: Front and rear platform wording
wording: Front ride-height platform helps define diffuser feed. Rear ride-height platform helps define diffuser outlet/expansion and scrape/choke behavior. Diffuser metrics are derived geometry proxies, not measured downforce.

title: CFS and front feed matter
wording: CFS/front ride-height platform evidence matters because the front platform helps define diffuser feed; read it with rear platform, scrape, speed loss, and derived diffuser proxy context.
do_not_say: rear ride height explains the whole aero state
CFS half-inch opening is accepted fact

title: Rear height is not alone
wording: Rear height alone does not determine rear aero behavior; read it with front feed, diffuser outlet/expansion context, scrape, and speed loss.
do_not_say: rear height alone proves the aero result

title: Front higher is contextual
wording: A front platform that is higher than the rear is not automatically wrong; the useful question is whether the feed, scrape margin, and speed trend agree.
do_not_say: front higher than rear is automatically wrong

title: Lower is contextual
wording: Lower is not automatically faster if it creates contact, unstable feed, or speed loss.

title: Proxy is not downforce
wording: Diffuser proxy channels are geometry-derived indicators for comparison and are not measured downforce.

title: Inspect combined platform
wording: Inspect CFS/front ride-height platform, rear ride-height platform, smooth rake, diffuser volume proxy, scrape, and speed loss together before naming a platform direction.
do_not_say: one channel proves the platform answer

title: Static rake is not enough
wording: Do not suggest ride-height, collar, or spring changes from static rake alone; require platform trace, scrape, and speed context.
do_not_say: static rake alone proves the setup direction

title: Smooth rake context
wording: Smooth rake is useful context only when combined with CFS/front platform, rear platform, diffuser volume proxy, scrape, and speed loss.
do_not_say: static rake alone proves the setup direction

title: Static rake sign is not the answer
wording: Static rake sign does not decide if a setup is good; inspect dynamic traces by zone with speed loss and scrape context.
do_not_say: static rake alone proves the setup direction

title: Inspect dynamic traces by zone
wording: Inspect platform, shock, tire, speed, and yaw traces in the same corner zone before naming a setup direction.
do_not_say: one whole-lap number proves the setup direction
